column1: # THE LOCK TABLE (GOH.LOCKORDER): every lock goh takes, in the ONE order they may nest.
# A process may WAIT on a lock only while every lock it (or an ancestor, GOH_HELD_LOCKS) holds has
# a LOWER rank: lib/lock_order.py and lib/lock_order.sh refuse the wait otherwise, naming both, and
# checks/check_lock_order.py derives the held-while-acquiring graph from the tree, sorts it
# topologically and goes red on a cycle or on an edge this order contradicts.
# Columns, tab-separated: name, rank, reentrant (a holder's own child may take it again: yes/no),
# scope (`repo`: one lock per repository; `machine`: one for the machine), the files that acquire it
# A `repo` lock of repository R is ordered only against the held locks taken in R (or in no known
# repository): a fixture repo's land lock inside another repo's gate is not that gate's lock

column6: the lands queue's one drainer, <landq>/lander.lock (never waits: a second drainer exits)
the idle lander's full suite on main's tip, <landq>/idle-suite/lock (never waits: a second idle run is skipped; the lander's own lock is released first)

the bump-only land of a ruff newer than goh's pin, <landq>/ruff-bump/lock (never waits: a second look while one bumps is busy; held across the bump's enqueue, whose pre-step waits only on higher ranks)
the one cache evictor's sweep, `<GOH_CACHE_EVICT_STATE>.lock` (GOH.CACHEEVICT; never waits: a second sweep exits 0), held while it try-locks cargo_build and head_cache
one goh ship per repository, <ship state>/.ship.lock, taken by tools/ship.py's worker (never waits: a second ship is refused, named by the holder it writes in it)
the repository's land queue, goh-land.lock in the common git dir; the ship's own release land is its holder's (GOH_LAND_LOCK_OWNER)
the load slot: an experiment (spinners) takes it alone; a 0-spinner run is a gate (gate_slot), and one inside a holder is that holder's
the quiet-machine reader-writer lock: every gate joins, a measurement takes it alone
the machine-wide gate slots, a counting semaphore every gate is admitted by (lib/admission.py admit: push gates, land gates through load.py 0); a gate nested in a holder takes none
one checkout's build tree (gates that wipe .build); lib/state_bounds.py only try-locks it, to keep a held run directory
the container runtime's lease table
the one screen
the GPU
one test's flake record and its 2-in-14-days filing, <flake register>/by-test/.<key>.flake.lock (GOH.FLAKEREGISTER): held around the read, the loopctl file and the appends (state_file, above it)

cargo's own `<build-dir>/<profile>/.cargo-build-lock` (`.cargo-lock` in a target dir), which cargo holds for a whole build: the evictor only ever try-locks it (taken: a live build holds the dir) and holds it across a demotion's copy or a delete's rename (the sweep's and lib/build_dir_reap.py's)
the load registry's own critical section (re-entrant within one process)
the estate registry file's read-modify-write
the cargo advisory database copy (shared to read, exclusive to refresh)
the HEAD-export cache
an eval transport's state file
the estate seed store directory
the machine-wide shellcheck tokens, a counting semaphore held around one shellcheck child (GOH.MEMADMIT)
the reuse audit's per-path state and counters, <reuse store>/audit.lock (GOH.REUSEAUDIT)
one live-share token of a run, <pool>/tok-<i> (GOH.SHAREGROW): a worker holds one per test; try-locks only, a worker without one polls
one bounded state ledger's sidecar lock, `.<name>.lock` beside it (GOH.LEDGERBOUND): every writer appends holding it shared, lib/state_bounds.py trims holding it alone (a try-lock)

one timing control at a time on the machine, <step-control cache>/.control.lock (GOH.RUSTCONTROLVOID): every land builds the same four cached copies, so two at once would each find the other's build fresh

goh.db (lib/goh_db.py, GOH.DBSEAM): SQLite's own write lock, BEGIN IMMEDIATE under busy_timeout. Innermost: it may be taken under any lock, and nothing is waited on while one is held (a transaction never spans a subprocess, an flock wait or a network call)
goh-cache.db (lib/goh_cache_db.py, GOH.DBSEAM): SQLite's own write lock, as goh_db's, ranked just inside it
